newsitem.title: UK: UK barley possible for Saudi buy but sourcing hard.
newsitem.headline: UK barley possible for Saudi buy but sourcing hard.

text.p: British barley could be used to supply some of the 500,000 tonnes Saudi Arabia is seeking under its latest tender, UK traders said.
But the problem is putting together enough grain to make a significant contribution. Asked if there was enough barley available, one shipper said "there certainly isn't in the south."
And there are plenty of alternative sources. "Barley's still cheap in Germany, and people are building up cargoes in France, as well as Rotterdam and Amsterdam," another said.
The problem is not necessarily that the UK does not have the barley, it is just finding it, an analyst explained.
"People keep saying there's barley out there, but it's on farm" he said. "It must be more scattered than ever."
Elements such as farmers' readiness to sell and their proximity to ports of loading came into play, he said. "Whether we could get it together at all is anybody's guess."

But the record value of sterling, which on Monday hit its highest level against the mark since September 1992, is not likely to be a handicap, one of the traders said. "I don't think that makes much difference. It's the physical impossibility of putting it together."

Saudia Arabia has launched an April 8 tender for 500,000 tonnes of barley of optional origin for delivery in a range of delivery periods ranging from the second half April to the second half of May, European grain traders said on Monday.
